tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. # Build New Preview Workflow

**Goal:** Turn user intent into a hardened, reviewable artifact.

**CRITICAL:** If a step directs you to another snapshot file, read it fully and follow it. No exceptions.

Subagents, when the capability is available, are an important part of this workflow. Use them as directed by the workflow steps.
If you need an explicit user instruction to run them, ask once now for the whole workflow run.

## READY FOR DEVELOPMENT STANDARD

A specification is "Ready for Development" when:

- **Actionable**: Every task has a file path and specific action.
- **Logical**: Tasks ordered by dependency.
- **Testable**: All ACs use Given/When/Then.
- **Complete**: No placeholders or TBDs.
- **Sufficient**: No known requirement, acceptance, dependency, or implementation gaps remain unresolved.
- **Coherent**: No unresolved ambiguities or internal contradictions.

## SCOPE STANDARD

A specification should target a **single user-facing goal** within **900–1600 tokens**:

- **Single goal**: One cohesive feature, even if it spans multiple layers/files. Multi-goal means >=2 **top-level independent shippable deliverables** — each could be reviewed, tested, and merged as a separate PR without breaking the others. Never count surface verbs, "and" conjunctions, or noun phrases. Never split cross-layer implementation details inside one user goal.
  - Split: "add dark mode toggle AND refactor auth to JWT AND build admin dashboard"
  - Don't split: "add validation and display errors" / "support drag-and-drop AND paste AND retry"
- **900–1600 tokens**: Optimal range for LLM consumption. Below 900 risks ambiguity; above 1600 risks context-rot in implementation agents.
- **Neither limit is a gate.** Both are proposals with user override.

## Conventions

- Every operational cross-file reference in this workflow is an absolute snapshot path. Open it directly; do not resolve it relative to a skill directory.
- `{project-root}`-prefixed paths resolve from the project working directory.
- Whenever this workflow captures or records a version-control revision, obtain the full canonical identifier directly from version control and preserve it verbatim.

- **Sequential Enforcement**: Complete steps in order, no skipping

Entrance is exactly `scrimIn` (0.18s ease-out fade) — the system's only other animation, `sheetUp`, is untouched.
- The authenticated screen's widget instance is never replaced across `authenticated`↔`expired` transitions — scroll/state preserved; the `AuthScreen` branch is unaffected.
- Copy never implies data loss; must state history/scroll position are preserved (mirrors the prototype's own "Sessão expirada" copy).

**Ask First:** if a future consumer needs a session state beyond this story's single new `expired` value, HALT before adding a fourth `SessionStatus` member — renegotiate the epic's AD first.

**Never:**
- No `go_router` — `main.dart` keeps its current `MaterialApp`/`Navigator` shape (Story 1.6).
- No Epic 2 biometric/PIN implementation — "Entrar novamente" only navigates to a throwaway placeholder that Epic 2 deletes wholesale.
- No new icon-font dependency — approximate the prototype's `ph-lock-key` with a built-in Material icon.
- No Reduce-Motion handling — out of this epic's scope.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Mid-session expiry | authenticated, any screen, any endpoint returns `AUTH_EXPIRED` | overlay appears over the current screen; its scroll/state is preserved | silent — no extra inline error |
| Already-open overlay | a second `AUTH_EXPIRED` arrives while the dialog is showing | no second dialog stacks | silent, single-overlay guard holds |
| Expiry while not authenticated | notifier fires but `_lastStatus != authenticated` (e.g. post-logout race) | no emission, no overlay | silent no-op |
| Boot-time refresh expiry | `restoreSession()`'s own `auth-refresh` call returns `AUTH_EXPIRED` | unchanged Story 1.4 behavior — lands on `AuthScreen`, never the overlay | existing path, untouched |
| "Entrar novamente" tapped | overlay visible | dialog dismissed, user routed to the biometric/PIN placeholder | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/core/session/session_expiry_notifier.dart` -- new: `SessionExpiryNotifier` port + broadcast-stream impl, pure Dart (no Flutter/feature import, RNF06) — the directory exists today as a Story 1.1 scaffold (`.gitkeep` only).
- `lib/core/network/api_client.dart:95-111` -- `_mapDioException` additionally calls `SessionExpiryNotifier.notifyExpired()` when the mapped failure `is AuthExpired` and `HeaderInterceptor.functionNameOf(e.requestOptions.path)` isn't in `anonKeyOnlyFunctions` (`header_interceptor.dart:20-24,80-83`) — new constructor dependency.
- `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart:33-61` -- register `SessionExpiryNotifier` as a singleton (with `dispose:`) before `ApiClient`; pass it into `ApiClient`'s constructor.
- `lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart` -- add third value `expired` to the current 2-value enum.
- `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart:27-140` -- constructor takes `SessionExpiryNotifier`; subscribes to `expiredEvents`, emits `SessionStatus.expired` per the "Always" guard above; cancels the subscription in `dispose()` (`:139`).
- `lib/features/auth/auth_injection.dart:33-39` -- pass `sessionExpiryNotifier: sl<SessionExpiryNotifier>()` into `SessionRepositoryImpl`.
- `lib/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog.dart` -- new shared component (UX-DR16): scrim + centered card, `titleColor` param (neutral here; Epic 8's account-deletion dialog later passes `colorError`), non-dismissible barrier, single-overlay guard, `scrimIn` entrance.
- `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` -- add `colorScrim` (see Design Notes) plus any new named spacing/padding constants the dialog card needs beyond the existing scale (RNF08).
- `lib/main.dart:90-132` -- `StreamBuilder` treats `authenticated`/`expired` as the same `_PostAuthPlaceholder` render; a small listener shows/dismisses `ConfirmationDialog` on that transition; new throwaway `_BiometricReauthPlaceholder` (same pattern as `_PostAuthPlaceholder`) is "Entrar novamente"'s target.

1	# Verification Gap Review
2	
3	**Goal:** Find changed behavior that could break without reliable verification catching it. Ask one question — "if the behavior this change is supposed to produce broke where it's actually used, would verification fail?" Do not hunt for correctness bugs, but report genuine problems you notice while tracing verification.
4	
5	The main verification gap shapes are:
6	
7	1. **Regression gap:** the changed code regresses where it's used, and no test covering that use would fail.
8	2. **Missing-adoption gap:** a place that should now use the new behavior doesn't; it handles the same case its own way, or not at all, and no test would flag the omission.
9	3. **Broken-verification gap:** a test appears to cover the changed behavior, but would not actually protect it because it is skipped, flaky, not run in the normal verification path, or too weak to observe the regression.
10	
11	## Evidence Rules
12	
13	- Read a test before claiming what it covers, runs, asserts, or misses.
14	- Before claiming no test exists, search the whole repo by the symbol under test and by import references; expected file locations are not enough.
15	- Never assert what you did not verify. If a finding cannot be grounded, drop it.
16	- In a finding, say what you actually checked — "none of the tests I read cover this" — and show how far you looked. Say a test doesn't exist anywhere only when the symbol/import-reference search actually shows that.
17	- Do not assign severity, confidence, priority, or ranking.
18	
19	## Review Sequence
20	
21	### Step 1: Screen for behavioral change
22	
23	Screen each part of the change separately. If a part is non-behavioral, skip it. Call a part non-behavioral only when the changed code does not alter return values, thrown errors, caller-visible side effects, or observable state (including iteration order and emitted messages). Once a part meets that test, move on; do not inspect callers or tests for extra confirmation.
24	
25	Common non-behavioral examples: formatting, comments, whitespace; pure renames; trivial getters/setters and pass-throughs; type-only or compiler-enforced changes with no runtime effect; etc.
26	
27	Only outcomes produced by deterministic code are worth automatically testing; tests are useless on static source text and brittle on LLM output. Skip those parts.
28	
29	If every part is skipped, output the clean result (see Output Format).
30	
31	### Step 2: Find the behavior that changed
32	
33	Identify what behavior changed compared to the previous version: output, side effect, branch, error path, schema/event shape, config default, validation/authorization rule, external contract, etc. If the change affects more than one behavior, handle each separately.
34	
35	Treat broad-impact changes as behavioral even when no single changed line looks important: dependency, toolchain, build/config, data-file, etc.
36	
37	### Step 3: Trace where that behavior is used
38	
39	Trace the changed behavior to the places that observe it. Start with direct callers and registered entry points (routes, commands, DI), contract consumers (schemas, events, APIs, database readers), and reverse-dependency info if already available.
40	
41	Follow a path only while the changed behavior is reachable and unverified. Stop when a test at that boundary would fail, the consumer does not observe the changed behavior, or the next hop is guesswork (dynamic dispatch, reflection, outside-repo consumers, etc.). Prefer the nearest observable boundary, often one to three hops away, especially across contract, integration, or service edges. If there are more than five similar consumers, group obvious repeats and check representative paths; expand only when a consumer observes the behavior differently.
42	
43	### Step 4: Qualify the consumer, then check its test
44	
45	For each consumer, name the smallest realistic regression this consumer would observe: invert the branch, drop the default, omit the field, return the old error code, skip the integration call, etc. This is the Demonstration. # Verification Gap Review

**Goal:** Find changed behavior that could break without reliable verification catching it. Ask one question — "if the behavior this change is supposed to produce broke where it's actually used, would verification fail?" Do not hunt for correctness bugs, but report genuine problems you notice while tracing verification.

The main verification gap shapes are:

1. **Regression gap:** the changed code regresses where it's used, and no test covering that use would fail.
2. **Missing-adoption gap:** a place that should now use the new behavior doesn't; it handles the same case its own way, or not at all, and no test would flag the omission.
3. **Broken-verification gap:** a test appears to cover the changed behavior, but would not actually protect it because it is skipped, flaky, not run in the normal verification path, or too weak to observe the regression.

## Evidence Rules

- Read a test before claiming what it covers, runs, asserts, or misses.
- Before claiming no test exists, search the whole repo by the symbol under test and by import references; expected file locations are not enough.
- Never assert what you did not verify. If a finding cannot be grounded, drop it.
- In a finding, say what you actually checked — "none of the tests I read cover this" — and show how far you looked. Say a test doesn't exist anywhere only when the symbol/import-reference search actually shows that.
- Do not assign severity, confidence, priority, or ranking.

## Review Sequence

### Step 1: Screen for behavioral change

Screen each part of the change separately. If a part is non-behavioral, skip it. Call a part non-behavioral only when the changed code does not alter return values, thrown errors, caller-visible side effects, or observable state (including iteration order and emitted messages). Once a part meets that test, move on; do not inspect callers or tests for extra confirmation.

Common non-behavioral examples: formatting, comments, whitespace; pure renames; trivial getters/setters and pass-throughs; type-only or compiler-enforced changes with no runtime effect; etc.

Only outcomes produced by deterministic code are worth automatically testing; tests are useless on static source text and brittle on LLM output. Skip those parts.

If every part is skipped, output the clean result (see Output Format).

### Step 2: Find the behavior that changed

Identify what behavior changed compared to the previous version: output, side effect, branch, error path, schema/event shape, config default, validation/authorization rule, external contract, etc. If the change affects more than one behavior, handle each separately.

Treat broad-impact changes as behavioral even when no single changed line looks important: dependency, toolchain, build/config, data-file, etc.

### Step 3: Trace where that behavior is used

Trace the changed behavior to the places that observe it. Start with direct callers and registered entry points (routes, commands, DI), contract consumers (schemas, events, APIs, database readers), and reverse-dependency info if already available.

Follow a path only while the changed behavior is reachable and unverified. Stop when a test at that boundary would fail, the consumer does not observe the changed behavior, or the next hop is guesswork (dynamic dispatch, reflection, outside-repo consumers, etc.). Prefer the nearest observable boundary, often one to three hops away, especially across contract, integration, or service edges. If there are more than five similar consumers, group obvious repeats and check representative paths; expand only when a consumer observes the behavior differently.

### Step 4: Qualify the consumer, then check its test

For each consumer, name the smallest realistic regression this consumer would observe: invert the branch, drop the default, omit the field, return the old error code, skip the integration call, etc. This is the Demonstration. If no such regression exists, drop the path; untested downstream code is not a finding.

A `Missing-adoption gap` qualifies not by the adoption failure alone but by a supersession signal: the change gives clear evidence the new behavior is meant to replace the local one — PR intent, naming or docs, a replaced sibling site, deleted duplicate logic, or a test defining the new rule — and the local site shares the same observable contract. Without a supersession signal and a shared observable contract, it is a refactor suggestion, not a verification-gap finding. Once both hold, check whether any test for that site would flag the non-adoption; missing coverage of the non-adoption is the gap itself, not a disqualifier.

Find and read the relevant test. Ask whether the Demonstration would make an assertion fail.

- If yes, the behavior is verified. No finding.
- For a regression-style Demonstration: if no test runs the path, the test is skipped/flaky/not run normally, or the test runs the code without checking the changed result, report a `Regression gap` or `Broken-verification gap`.
- For a qualifying Missing-adoption case: if none of the site tests you found assert it adopts the new behavior, report a `Missing-adoption gap`.

A test counts only if it runs normally and an assertion observes the changed output, branch, or contract. These do not count: no execution; source-text assertions that match a file's wording instead of running it; success/no-throw/snapshot-only checks; mock/log-call checks; human-only checks; tests that mock away the integration; e2e tests that pass through without checking the changed output; stale assertions or fixtures.

For example, `expect(x ?? DEFAULT).toBe(DEFAULT)` passes when `x` is missing.

Common patterns:

- **Caller-path gap** — helper test covers the branch, but caller values skip it.
- **Contract drift** — payload/schema/event changes must be verified at the consumer.
- **Migration compatibility** — tests only create new-format rows or fresh schemas.
- **Phantom exception** — handled partial-failure path has no test.
- **Missing-adoption gap** — sibling site should use the new rule/helper and does not.
- **Removed verification** — deleted test or weakened assertion leaves behavior unpinned; removing a source-text assertion is not this, since it never counted.

### Step 5: Confirm each finding is real

Before writing a finding, re-open the specific tests or search results the finding relies on. Verify the Demonstration would not make any test you checked fail, or that the absence claim is backed by the symbol/import-reference search. Do not claim more than you verified; drop any finding you cannot ground.

Explain why the test misses the bug using what the test sets up and checks.

Do not report: compiler/type-checker-enforced cases; behavior already verified by an integration, contract, or e2e test; implementation-detail or mock-only tests; low coverage or a missing test file by itself; legacy untested code the change did not affect.

Report genuine problems you noticed while tracing verification, even if they are not verification gaps. Put them under `Other findings` in the output. This permits reporting what you already reached, not extra hunting.

## OUTPUT FORMAT

Emit each verification-gap finding as one block. No general advice, no severity or confidence.

```markdown
### <one-line title naming the gap>

- **Changed surface:** the exact behavior or contract that changed — `file:line`.
- **Impacted consumer or site:** named concretely with `file:line` (e.g. "the `createInvoice` mutation used by the billing dashboard at `billing/dashboard.ts:88`," not "callers of this function").
- **Existing test evidence:**
  - `Regression gap`: what the relevant test actually asserts, with `file:line`; or, if none, the symbol/import-reference searches run and their result.
  - `Missing-adoption gap`: tests for the impacted site, and whether any assert it adopts the new behavior.
  - `Broken-verification gap`: the apparent test or verification path, and why it does not count.
- **Missing verification:** the precise assertion or check that's absent.
- **Demonstration:**
  - `Regression gap` / `Broken-verification gap`: the concrete regression that would ship undetected, and why the tests you checked would not fail.
  - `Missing-adoption gap`: the case the site mishandles by not adopting the new behavior, and that none of the tests you read assert adoption.
- **Consequence:** the concrete thing that ships wrong — a regression the checked evidence would not catch, or a site that should use the new behavior and doesn't.
- **Suggested test shape:** (optional) the kind of test that would close the gap, fit to the repo's own way of verifying — don't impose a generic test pyramid.
```

If you noticed genuine non-gap problems while tracing verification, append:

```markdown
## Other findings

- <description only; no severity, confidence, priority, or ranking>
```

When you find no verification gaps and no other findings, output exactly this single line, not an empty response:

`No verification gaps found.`

## CONTENT SOURCE

Review the content supplied under "Review content:" in the message that launched you. If none is supplied, stop with exactly: `No verification gaps found.`

diff --git a/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/deferred-work.md b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/deferred-work.md

@@ -35,9 +35,5 @@
 ## Deferred from: code review of story-1-4-silent-session-refresh-persistence (2026-10-27)
 
 - source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-1-4-silent-session-refresh-persistence.md`
-  summary: `AuthCubit.toggleMode()`'s uncommitted fix (switched from a raw `AuthState(...)` constructor to `state.copyWith(...)` so an in-flight `status` survives a mode toggle) has no test that can actually observe the regression it fixes — every existing `toggleMode()` call site in the test suite toggles while `status` is already the default idle value.
-  evidence: Root cause is in `lib/features/auth/presentation/cubit/auth_cubit.dart`, pre-existing uncommitted work carried over from story 1.3's review loop, not touched by story 1.4's diff — surfaced incidentally by story 1.4's review because the dirty working tree put it in the reviewed diff. Needs a test that calls `submit()` to put `status` in a non-idle state, then `toggleMode()`, then asserts `status` is unchanged.
-
-- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-1-4-silent-session-refresh-persistence.md`
-  summary: `AuthCubit.passwordChanged()`'s uncommitted fix (now also clears `emailError`, matching `emailChanged`'s existing symmetric clear) has no test asserting it actually clears a pre-existing e-mail error.
-  evidence: Same pre-existing-uncommitted-work category as the `toggleMode` entry above (`lib/features/auth/presentation/cubit/auth_cubit.dart`, carried over from story 1.3's review loop) — not caused by story 1.4. Needs a test that first drives `emailError` non-null (e.g. a failed local-validation submit with a malformed e-mail), then calls `passwordChanged`, then asserts `emailError` is now null.
+  summary: `AuthCubit.toggleMode()`'s `state.copyWith(...)` fix (so an in-flight `status` survives a mode toggle, instead of the previous raw `AuthState(...)` constructor silently resetting it) has no test that can actually observe the regression it fixes — every existing `toggleMode()` call site in the test suite toggles while `status` is already the default idle value.
+  evidence: Code review of story-1-4 corrected this entry's earlier "not touched by story 1.4's diff" claim — the change to `lib/features/auth/presentation/cubit/auth_cubit.dart` IS part of this diff. It's deferred on its own merits instead: `toggleMode()`'s only call site is a button disabled whenever `isSubmitting` is true, and every submit-failure path resets `status` back to idle in the same `emit` that sets `formError` — so there is no path through the real `AuthScreen` that can currently drive `status` non-idle at the moment `toggleMode()` runs. Needs a test that calls `submit()` to put `status` in a non-idle state, then `toggleMode()`, then asserts `status` is unchanged — revisit if a future change makes that sequence reachable.

 - Given the text field error state, when rendered, then the border is 1.5px `colorError`.
 - Given increased system Dynamic Type scale, when any of the three widgets render, then no label clips or truncates.
 
+### Review Findings
+
+- [x] [Review][Patch] Remove unreachable `disabledBorder` in `AppTextField` — no `enabled` param exists to ever trigger it [lib/core/widgets/app_text_field.dart:81]
+- [x] [Review][Patch] Run `dart format` on the three new widget files — not formatter-clean as committed [lib/core/widgets/app_button.dart, lib/core/widgets/app_text_field.dart, lib/core/widgets/avatar.dart]
+- [x] [Review][Defer] `AppButton` has no loading/busy state for async call sites (login submit, "Salvar", export actions) [lib/core/widgets/app_button.dart] — deferred, pre-existing
+- [x] [Review][Defer] `AppTextField` lacks `enabled`/`readOnly`/`onSubmitted`/`autofocus`/`textCapitalization`/`inputFormatters` — first real consumer (Story 1.3) should request what it needs [lib/core/widgets/app_text_field.dart] — deferred, pre-existing
+- [x] [Review][Defer] `design_tokens.dart` now imports `package:flutter/widgets.dart` with no lint/architecture test guarding a future `domain/` layer from importing it (RNF06 risk) [lib/core/design_tokens.dart:1] — deferred, pre-existing
+- [x] [Review][Decision] New `component_library_interaction_test.dart` harness's narrative is built on a false premise ("story 1.3's screen doesn't exist yet" — it already shipped in `8a4b944`) — resolved: **keep the file**. Checked whether `auth_screen_test.dart` (BLoC/cubit-focused, 294 lines) actually duplicates it: it never exercises `obscureText`, keyboard-action focus movement, or a direct `onPressed`/disabled-callback assertion — this harness is the only coverage of those shared-widget interaction behaviors, decoupled from any one screen's BLoC wiring. Reframing (see patch below) rather than deleting.
+- [x] [Review][Patch] Correct `test-summary.md`'s Context section — remove the false "story 1.3 owns the first real screen... a story ahead of when that screen actually exists" framing (Story 1.3 already shipped beneath this diff); reframe the harness as a dedicated core-widget composition/interaction test that covers what `auth_screen_test.dart`'s BLoC-focused suite does not (obscured senha, keyboard-action focus movement, direct disabled-callback behavior) [_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/tests/test-summary.md]
+- [x] [Review][Patch] Run `dart format` on the new test file — not formatter-clean as added [test/core/widgets/component_library_interaction_test.dart]
+- [x] [Review][Patch] Correct the stale test count in `test-summary.md`'s Verification section — now 169/169 (161 pre-existing + 8 new, including the new error-recovery test added below) [_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/tests/test-summary.md]
+- [x] [Review][Patch] Override `dispose()` in `_LoginShapedFormState` to release `_emailController`, `_senhaController`, and `_senhaFocus` [test/core/widgets/component_library_interaction_test.dart]
+- [x] [Review][Patch] Add a test for the error-recovery flow — correcting an invalid e-mail and resubmitting now has its own test asserting the error clears and `onSubmit` fires [test/core/widgets/component_library_interaction_test.dart]
+- [x] [Review][Patch] Assert the invalid-email error border's width (`DesignTokens.borderWidthEmphasis`), not just its color — the spec's own AC is "1.5px `colorError` border" [test/core/widgets/component_library_interaction_test.dart]
+- [x] [Review][Patch] Make the disabled-button test assert `onPressed == null` directly and count callback invocations, instead of only checking the absence of an unrelated error text as a side effect [test/core/widgets/component_library_interaction_test.dart]
+- [x] [Review][Patch] Removed the `Avatar(initials: 'WD')` from the harness — the real login screen (`auth_screen.dart`) and the prototype's Tela 0.1a show no avatar on a pre-authentication screen with no known user identity yet [test/core/widgets/component_library_interaction_test.dart]
+- [x] [Review][Defer] Senha field sets `textInputAction: TextInputAction.done` but `AppTextField` has no `onSubmitted` param to wire a handler to it [test/core/widgets/component_library_interaction_test.dart, lib/core/widgets/app_text_field.dart] — deferred, pre-existing (already tracked in `deferred-work.md`'s story-1-3 review entry)
+
 ## Spec Change Log
 
 - **Review round 1 (patch findings, no spec-level change):** three parallel reviews (blind-hunter, edge-case-hunter, verification-gap) surfaced 6 distinct patchable gaps, all fixed in place: (1) added a `DesignTokens — layout insets` test group for `buttonPadding`/`textFieldContentPadding`/`avatarInitialsPadding`, previously untested; (2) added a `side.resolve({disabled})` assertion to `AppButton`'s secondaryOutline disabled test; (3) `AppButton.secondaryOutline`'s `BorderSide` now passes `width: DesignTokens.borderWidthDefault` explicitly instead of silently falling back to Flutter's default (RNF08 literal bypass); (4) documented the button-corner-radius decision below (was undocumented); (5) corrected `AppTextField.errorText`'s doc comment, which overstated the contract ("non-null and non-empty") beyond the frozen spec's actual `errorText != null` condition; (6) added `radiusSm` assertions to the `AppButton` primary and `AppTextField` default-state tests. Rejected as non-issues: `textColor` no-op on non-ghost variants (documented by design), `Avatar` empty-initials fallback (caller's responsibility per its own doc), missing pressed-overlay on secondary/ghost (prototype never defines one), barrel file/a11y/form-hooks suggestions (deferred or out of scope, see `deferred-work.md`).

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

# Test Automation Summary

## Context

Cerne has no device/simulator or CI pipeline yet (AGENTS.md), so a true
platform-level E2E (`integration_test` on a real/simulated device) isn't
viable right now. The project already substitutes composition-root widget
tests — `CerneApp` pumped with only a single named boundary faked (the
`AuthRepository`/`SessionRepository` interface, or, in
`network_pipeline_integration_test.dart`, the `HttpClientAdapter`) — as its
E2E equivalent. `ApiClient`'s own docstring states the convention
explicitly: tests mock `ApiClient` directly; only one dedicated suite is
allowed to fake the transport boundary beneath it. All API-level coverage
(status codes, response mapping, the 3-error write-failure matrix per
write endpoint, retry behavior, header/URL building) already exists across
`test/core/network/` and `test/features/auth/data/`.

Before adding anything, the full suite was run: **194/194 tests passing**,
`flutter analyze`: **0 issues**. Given that density, the only legitimate
gap found was in the composition-root (E2E-equivalent) layer.

## Generated Tests

### E2E Tests (composition-root, `test/main_test.dart`)

- [x] `test/main_test.dart` — **new**: "CerneApp resolves the real AuthCubit
  and navigates to the post-auth placeholder once signup succeeds" —
  mirrors the existing real-wiring login test, but drives the
  toggle-to-signup path. Previously, signup was only exercised against a
  directly-constructed `AuthScreen`/`AuthCubit` pair
  (`auth_screen_test.dart`), never through `main.dart`'s actual
  `sl<AuthCubit>()` resolution and `onAuthenticated` → `Navigator`
  wiring — only the login path had that proof.

No other E2E or API gaps were found; everything else implemented so far
(design tokens/component library, auth validators, auth cubit, auth
repository/data source, session repository, network pipeline, DI bootstrap)
already has dedicated coverage at the appropriate layer.

## Coverage

- Composition-root E2E scenarios: login ✅, **signup ✅ (added)**,
  authenticated-boot ✅, unauthenticated-boot ✅, boot-loading-threshold ✅
- API/data-source coverage: auth-login, auth-signup, auth-refresh — happy
  path + the full 3-case write-failure matrix (timeout/malformed/offline)
  each, plus retry and non-retry behavior proven over a faked transport
- Implemented feature scope (per `sprint-status.yaml`): stories 1.1–1.4
  (scaffold, design tokens, auth, session refresh) — all covered. Stories
  1.5+ are still `backlog`, so out of scope for this pass.

## Verification

- `fvm flutter test` → 195/195 passing (194 pre-existing + 1 new)
- `fvm flutter analyze` → 0 issues

## Next Steps

- Revisit the "no device/CI" constraint (AGENTS.md) once a simulator or CI
  step exists — at that point, a real `integration_test` driver test
  becomes possible and composition-root tests can be retired in its favor.
- Re-run this pass after each future story (1.5 expired-session overlay,
  1.6 navigation shell, …) lands, since each adds a new composition-root
  surface worth the same login/signup-style proof.

# Story 1.5 — Expired-Session Recovery Overlay

## Context

Story 1.5 adds a new core port (`SessionExpiryNotifier`), a third
`SessionStatus` value (`expired`), a new shared `ConfirmationDialog`
overlay widget, and `main.dart`'s reaction to the two together. Each new
unit gets its own isolated test, and the composition-root suite
(`test/main_test.dart`) gets the end-to-end proof that a mid-session
`AUTH_EXPIRED` actually surfaces the overlay over the live screen and
routes on confirm — same E2E-equivalent pattern this file's Story 1.4
section established.

Code review of this story's own diff surfaced and fixed four gaps before
landing: a rebuild that could reopen an already-dismissed overlay (no
guard against calling `show()` more than once per `expired` episode), the
system back gesture being able to dismiss the overlay despite the
non-dismissible-barrier requirement (`PopScope` was missing), a synchronous
`showGeneralDialog` failure permanently locking the single-overlay guard,
and a stored-but-empty refresh token not short-circuiting
`restoreSession()` the same way a `null` one does.

## Generated Tests

### Unit (new core/feature code)

- [x] `test/core/session/session_expiry_notifier_test.dart` — **new**:
  `SessionExpiryNotifierImpl.notifyExpired()`/`expiredEvents`/`dispose()`.
- [x] `test/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl_test.dart`
  — **extended**: the `expired` bridge's whole I/O matrix (mid-session
  expiry while authenticated, while unauthenticated, before any status
  yet, a second event while already `expired`, `dispose()` cancelling the
  subscription), plus a stored-but-empty refresh token now being treated
  as "no session" the same as `null`.
- [x] `test/core/network/api_client_test.dart` — **extended**: the
  notifier fires only for a mid-session `AUTH_EXPIRED` outside
  `anonKeyOnlyFunctions`.
- [x] `test/core/network/network_pipeline_integration_test.dart` —
  **extended**: an `AUTH_EXPIRED` response on a bearer call reaches the
  notifier through the real wiring, not just the mocked `ApiClient` unit.

### Composition/interaction (shared widget)

- [x] `test/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog_test.dart` — **new**: neutral
  vs. destructive `titleColor`, the non-dismissible scrim (including a
  dedicated check that the tap is actually absorbed by the barrier rather
  than just leaving the dialog on screen), the back-gesture `PopScope`
  guard, the single-overlay guard, `onConfirm` firing, focus staying
  trapped on the dialog under Tab traversal, and no overflow at 3.0x
  Dynamic Type.

### E2E Tests (composition-root, `test/main_test.dart`)

- [x] `test/main_test.dart` — **extended**, new "Story 1.5" group: the
  overlay appearing over the still-mounted authenticated screen, a second
  `expired` emission never stacking a second dialog, "Entrar novamente"
  dismissing the overlay and routing to the biometric/PIN placeholder, and
  a later rebuild while `statusStream` is still `expired` (simulated by
  pumping the same `CerneApp` root again) not reopening an
  already-confirmed overlay.

## Coverage

- Composition-root E2E scenarios: mid-session expiry overlay ✅, no
  second overlay on a repeat event ✅, confirm-and-route ✅, no reopen on
  an unrelated rebuild ✅ (added)
- Core/unit coverage: `SessionExpiryNotifier`, the `expired` bridge's full
  I/O matrix, `ConfirmationDialog`'s accessibility/dismissal guarantees —
  all covered at the layer where coverage is cheapest and clearest.
- Implemented feature scope (per `sprint-status.yaml`): stories 1.1–1.5 —
  all covered. Story 1.6 is still `backlog`, so out of scope for this pass.

## Verification

- `fvm flutter test` → 223/223 passing (195 pre-existing + 28 new/extended)
- `fvm flutter analyze` → 0 issues

## Next Steps

- When Story 1.6 (base navigation shell) replaces `main.dart`'s
  `MaterialApp`/`Navigator` shape with `go_router`, re-home this story's
  composition-root assertions onto whatever replaces `_CerneAppState`.
- Epic 2's real biometric/PIN re-auth flow is the first thing that will
  need to transition `SessionStatus` back out of `expired` — extend this
  story's bridge coverage there rather than re-deriving it (tracked in
  `deferred-work.md`).

`SessionStatus` value (`expired`), a new shared `ConfirmationDialog`
overlay widget, and `main.dart`'s reaction to the two together. Each new

landing: a rebuild that could reopen an already-dismissed overlay (no
guard against calling `show()` more than once per `expired` episode), the
system back gesture being able to dismiss the overlay despite the
non-dismissible-barrier requirement (`PopScope` was missing), a synchronous

# Test Automation Summary

## Context

Cerne has no device/simulator or CI pipeline yet (AGENTS.md), so a true
platform-level E2E (`integration_test` on a real/simulated device) isn't

`test/core/network/` and `test/features/auth/data/`.

gap found was in the composition-root (E2E-equivalent) layer.

input.new_string:
- Given `fvm flutter analyze`, when run after this change, then zero issues and no hardcoded `Color(0x`/`EdgeInsets.*` literal outside `design_tokens.dart`.

### Review Findings

- [x] [Review][Patch] `session_status.dart`'s doc comment grammar: "never a extra enum value" -> "never an extra enum value" [lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart:4]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `main.dart`'s `_maybeShowExpiryOverlay` could reopen an already-confirmed-and-dismissed overlay on any later rebuild that still observes `expired` (nothing transitions the status away from it) — `ConfirmationDialog.isOpen` alone only guards against *concurrent* stacking, not a reopen after the first close. Fixed with a separate one-shot-per-episode `_expiryOverlayShown` flag on `_CerneAppState`. [lib/main.dart]
- [x] [Review][Patch] The overlay's non-dismissible requirement (UX-DR16/25/27/36) only blocked a scrim tap (`barrierDismissible: false`) — the system/hardware back gesture could still pop the route and dismiss it. Fixed by wrapping the dialog's route content in `PopScope(canPop: false, ...)`. [lib/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog.dart]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `ConfirmationDialog.show()` set `isOpen = true` before calling `showGeneralDialog`, with no guard against a synchronous throw (e.g. a future caller passing a context with no `Navigator` ancestor) — would permanently lock the app-wide single-overlay guard. Fixed with a try/catch that resets `isOpen` and rethrows. [lib/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog.dart]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `SessionRepositoryImpl`'s `_expirySubscription.listen(...)` had no `onError`, unlike `statusStream`'s own internal subscription a few lines below — a future `SessionExpiryNotifier` implementation that ever errored would surface as an unhandled zone exception. Fixed with a matching `onError: (_, _) {}`. [lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `main.dart`'s `onConfirm` closure re-used its captured outer `context` to push the biometric placeholder without re-checking `context.mounted` immediately before the call (only checked once, at the point the overlay was scheduled). Unreachable today (nothing can unmount `_PostAuthPlaceholder` while the dialog is open), but cheap to guard. Fixed with a second `mounted` check inside `onConfirm`. [lib/main.dart]
- [x] [Review][Patch] No test covered a stored-but-empty refresh token on `restoreSession()` — the `refreshToken == null || refreshToken.isEmpty` short-circuit added by this diff had no regression coverage. Fixed with a new test case. [test/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl_test.dart]
- [x] [Review][Patch] The `dispose()` subscription-cancel test only asserted `expiryController.add(null)` didn't throw — that's true regardless of whether `_expirySubscription.cancel()` actually ran (the `_emit()` `isClosed` guard added by this same diff swallows the result either way), so it couldn't actually catch a regression. Fixed by asserting no event reaches `statusStream` after dispose. [test/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl_test.dart]
- [x] [Review][Patch] No test covered the Boundaries' "focus-trapped" requirement for `ConfirmationDialog`. Fixed with a Tab-traversal test asserting a background `TextField` never gains focus while the overlay is open. [test/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog_test.dart]
- [x] [Review][Patch] The existing "tapping the scrim does nothing" test only re-asserted the dialog's title text was still present — it would keep passing even if the tap missed everything entirely (e.g. if the card ever grew to cover that corner), not just if the barrier genuinely absorbed it. Fixed by adding a dedicated test with a background `GestureDetector` that proves the tap never reaches it. [test/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog_test.dart]
- [x] [Review][Defer] Nothing transitions `SessionStatus` back from `expired` to `authenticated` anywhere — by design for this story (Epic 2's real re-auth owns that), but it wasn't recorded as a known future obligation the way this diff's own `toggleMode` gap is. Recorded in `deferred-work.md`. [lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart, lib/main.dart] — deferred, Epic 2's concern

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** `ApiClient._mapDioException` already maps any mid-session `AUTH_EXPIRED` response to `Failure.authExpired` (`api_client.dart:95-111`), but nothing reacts to it — `SessionStatus` only ever emits from the boot-time `restoreSession()` call (`session_repository_impl.dart:81-136`), so an expired session mid-use today surfaces only as a raw inline error on whatever screen made the call, and the user is never routed back to re-auth.

**Approach:** Add a core `SessionExpiryNotifier` port (in the already-scaffolded empty `lib/core/session/`) that `ApiClient` signals on any non-boot `AUTH_EXPIRED`; `SessionRepositoryImpl` bridges that into one new `SessionStatus.expired` value on the epic's existing single stream. `main.dart` keeps rendering the same authenticated screen across that transition and shows a new shared `ConfirmationDialog` overlay (neutral title) whose "Entrar novamente" button routes to a throwaway re-auth placeholder standing in for Epic 2's biometric/PIN flow.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `ApiClient` notifies expiry only for `AUTH_EXPIRED` on calls outside `HeaderInterceptor.anonKeyOnlyFunctions` (`header_interceptor.dart:20-24`, matched via its `functionNameOf`) — boot-time `auth-refresh` keeps going through Story 1.4's existing `restoreSession()` path untouched.
- `SessionStatus` gains exactly one new `expired` value; `statusStream`/`restoreSession`/`dispose` signatures are unchanged — still the epic's one singleton stream (AD), no second stream.
- `SessionRepositoryImpl` emits `expired` only when `_lastStatus == SessionStatus.authenticated`; any other current status ignores the event (no spurious overlay during boot or after logout).
- Overlay = new `ConfirmationDialog` (`lib/core/widgets/`): neutral `colorTextPrimary` title (never `colorError`), non-dismissible barrier, focus-trapped, at most one open at a time (UX-DR16/25/27/36). Entrance is exactly `scrimIn` (0.18s ease-out fade) — the system's only other animation, `sheetUp`, is untouched.
- The authenticated screen's widget instance is never replaced across `authenticated`↔`expired` transitions — scroll/state preserved; the `AuthScreen` branch is unaffected.
- Copy never implies data loss; must state history/scroll position are preserved (mirrors the prototype's own "Sessão expirada" copy).

**Ask First:** if a future consumer needs a session state beyond this story's single new `expired` value, HALT before adding a fourth `SessionStatus` member — renegotiate the epic's AD first.

**Never:**
- No `go_router` — `main.dart` keeps its current `MaterialApp`/`Navigator` shape (Story 1.6).
- No Epic 2 biometric/PIN implementation — "Entrar novamente" only navigates to a throwaway placeholder that Epic 2 deletes wholesale.
- No new icon-font dependency — approximate the prototype's `ph-lock-key` with a built-in Material icon.
- No Reduce-Motion handling — out of this epic's scope.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Mid-session expiry | authenticated, any screen, any endpoint returns `AUTH_EXPIRED` | overlay appears over the current screen; its scroll/state is preserved | silent — no extra inline error |
| Already-open overlay | a second `AUTH_EXPIRED` arrives while the dialog is showing | no second dialog stacks | silent, single-overlay guard holds |
| Expiry while not authenticated | notifier fires but `_lastStatus != authenticated` (e.g. post-logout race) | no emission, no overlay | silent no-op |
| Boot-time refresh expiry | `restoreSession()`'s own `auth-refresh` call returns `AUTH_EXPIRED` | unchanged Story 1.4 behavior — lands on `AuthScreen`, never the overlay | existing path, untouched |
| "Entrar novamente" tapped | overlay visible | dialog dismissed, user routed to the biometric/PIN placeholder | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/core/session/session_expiry_notifier.dart` -- new: `SessionExpiryNotifier` port + broadcast-stream impl, pure Dart (no Flutter/feature import, RNF06) — the directory exists today as a Story 1.1 scaffold (`.gitkeep` only).
- `lib/core/network/api_client.dart:95-111` -- `_mapDioException` additionally calls `SessionExpiryNotifier.notifyExpired()` when the mapped failure `is AuthExpired` and `HeaderInterceptor.functionNameOf(e.requestOptions.path)` isn't in `anonKeyOnlyFunctions` (`header_interceptor.dart:20-24,80-83`) — new constructor dependency.
- `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart:33-61` -- register `SessionExpiryNotifier` as a singleton (with `dispose:`) before `ApiClient`; pass it into `ApiClient`'s constructor.
- `lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart` -- add third value `expired` to the current 2-value enum.
- `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart:27-140` -- constructor takes `SessionExpiryNotifier`; subscribes to `expiredEvents`, emits `SessionStatus.expired` per the "Always" guard above; cancels the subscription in `dispose()` (`:139`).
- `lib/features/auth/auth_injection.dart:33-39` -- pass `sessionExpiryNotifier: sl<SessionExpiryNotifier>()` into `SessionRepositoryImpl`.
- `lib/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog.dart` -- new shared component (UX-DR16): scrim + centered card, `titleColor` param (neutral here; Epic 8's account-deletion dialog later passes `colorError`), non-dismissible barrier, single-overlay guard, `scrimIn` entrance.
- `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` -- add `colorScrim` (see Design Notes) plus any new named spacing/padding constants the dialog card needs beyond the existing scale (RNF08).
- `lib/main.dart:90-132` -- `StreamBuilder` treats `authenticated`/`expired` as the same `_PostAuthPlaceholder` render; a small listener shows/dismisses `ConfirmationDialog` on that transition; new throwaway `_BiometricReauthPlaceholder` (same pattern as `_PostAuthPlaceholder`) is "Entrar novamente"'s target.
- Ground truth for copy/visuals: `docs/input/prototype/cerne-prototype.html` ("OVERLAY: Sessão expirada" block) and `prototype-extract.md:69,174-176,227`; `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md:7` (`AUTH_EXPIRED`, 401, non-retryable).

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**

- [x] `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` -- call the notifier on mid-session `AUTH_EXPIRED` -- the one detection point (AD-2/AD-5)
- [x] `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart` -- register + wire the notifier into `ApiClient` -- DI
- [x] `lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart` -- add `expired` -- the signal `main.dart` branches on
- [x] `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart` -- bridge the notifier into `statusStream` -- epic AD, one stream only
- [x] `lib/features/auth/auth_injection.dart` -- wire the notifier into `SessionRepositoryImpl` -- DI
- [x] `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` -- add `colorScrim` + any new dialog-card constants -- RNF08
- [x] `lib/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog.dart` -- new shared overlay component -- UX-DR16/25/27/36
- [x] `lib/main.dart` -- show/dismiss the overlay across `authenticated`↔`expired` without replacing the screen; add `_BiometricReauthPlaceholder`
- [x] `test/core/session/session_expiry_notifier_test.dart` -- new -- notify/listen/dispose
- [x] `test/core/network/api_client_test.dart` -- extend -- notifies only on non-anon-key-function `AUTH_EXPIRED`
- [x] `test/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl_test.dart` -- extend -- `expired` only fires from `authenticated`
- [x] `test/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog_test.dart` -- new -- neutral title color, non-dismissible barrier, single-overlay guard, Dynamic Type
- [x] `test/main_test.dart` -- extend -- overlay appears/dismisses without losing the underlying screen; "Entrar novamente" routes to the placeholder

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the overlay is open, when the user taps the scrim, then nothing happens (barrier is non-dismissible, focus stays trapped on the dialog).
- Given `fvm flutter analyze`, when run after this change, then zero issues and no hardcoded `Color(0x`/`EdgeInsets.*` literal outside `design_tokens.dart`.

## Design Notes

- `colorScrim` must be `Color(0x38241F19)` — `rgba(36,31,25,.22)`, the exact value `cerne-prototype.html` uses for *this* overlay specifically. Its other overlays (drawer, insertion modal, filter/export sheets, account-deletion confirm) use `rgba(36,31,25,.4)` (`0x66...`) instead — don't reuse that heavier value here; it belongs to whichever later story builds those.
- `SessionExpiryNotifier` lives in core (not the auth feature) specifically so `ApiClient` can signal expiry without importing anything from `features/auth` (RNF06) — `SessionRepositoryImpl` is the one bridge back onto the single `SessionStatus` stream.

# Sync Sprint Status

Shared sub-step for updating `sprint-status.yaml` during build. Called from any route (plan-code-review, one-shot, future routes) with a `target_status` parameter.

## Preconditions

Skip this entire file (return to caller) if ANY of:
- `story_key` is unset
- `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/sprint-status.yaml` does not exist on disk

## Instructions

1. Load the FULL `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/sprint-status.yaml` file.
2. Find the `development_status` entry matching `{story_key}`. If not found, warn the user once (`"{story_key} not found in sprint-status; skipping sprint sync"`) and return to caller.
3. **Idempotency check.** If `development_status[{story_key}]` is already at `target_status` or a later state (`review` is later than `in-progress`; `done` is later than both), return to caller — no write needed. Never regress a story's status.
4. Set `development_status[{story_key}]` to `{target_status}`.
5. **Epic lift (only when `target_status` = `in-progress`).** Derive the parent epic key as `epic-{N}` from the leading numeric segment of `{story_key}` (e.g., `3-2-digest-delivery` → `epic-3`). If that entry exists and is `backlog`, set it to `in-progress`. Leave it alone otherwise. Skip this sub-step entirely when `target_status` is not `in-progress`.
6. Refresh `last_updated` to the current date.
7. Save the file, preserving ALL comments and structure including STATUS DEFINITIONS and WORKFLOW NOTES.
